name: Tethered Cord Syndrome
definition: Neurological syndrome caused by pathological traction on the spinal cord, congenital or acquired, often associated with spinal dysraphism.

investigations.principle: MRI lumbosacral spine is the principal study; urodynamics may be used when bladder dysfunction is suspected.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Surgical untethering is considered for progressive or clearly symptomatic tethering.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vata/neurodevelopmental phenotype may be documented only as a parallel layer.

patientEducation.summary: Neurological syndrome caused by pathological traction on the spinal cord, congenital or acquired, often associated with spinal dysraphism.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
